_readme: Copy to <server>/UserData/rtsai.json. READ ONLY — the mod never writes it,
so unlike MelonPreferences.cfg an edit survives a shutdown, and it is re-read
at every map load, so an edit takes effect on the NEXT ROUND with the server
Every key is optional. Delete a line and the MelonPreferences value applies.
Delete the whole file and nothing changes at all.
While the A/B rig is cycling arms, the rig owns workerCapPerBioCache and
producerPerSites — those keys are ignored and the log says so once. Set
configCycle to 'off' to steer them from here instead.
_autoResourceDrain: false (default) — cash is left alone. At capacity the game clamps it, so
income stops accruing and cumulIncome reads as money that really existed.
true — cash is cut to 70% of team capacity whenever it passes 75%, and
cumulIncome credits what was drained. That makes the benchmark measure
EARNING POWER past the cap, at the price of destroying the money: it took
315k out of a 988k NarakaCity round on 2026-08-06. Only for measurement.
Capacity is roughly 4,000 per Bio Cache, so the cap moves with the base.
_pileUp: Anti-pile-up. Displaced shrimps each picked their own nearest free patch,
blind to the ones that just went there — so a depletion cascade sent all of
them to the same ground (56 on a patch with capacity 7, NarakaCity
2026-08-07) while the middle and west of the map sat empty.
pileUpMaxPerPatch — shrimps that may be WALKING to one destination at once.
The 11th takes the next-best patch instead. 0 disables the mechanism and
restores nearest-wins. 10 matches the per-Bio-Cache worker cap.
pileUpMaxDetourM — how much further a spilled shrimp may be sent once its
first choice is full. 0 = no limit, which is the intent: a long walk to
fresh ground beats standing on a dead patch. Raise off 0 only if a map
punishes the walk more than the pile-up.
_storageBuffer: A pile of FREE Bio Caches spawned beside the Nest at a fixed minute, purely
to raise team storage capacity so income stops clipping at the cap.
Capacity is ~4,000 per Bio Cache, so 100 caches ~ +400,000.
They are SPAWNED (admin path): no cost, no build time, no placement checks,
stacked on one spot. They measure nothing about the bot's expansion and are
excluded from bc_metrics and the per-Bio-Cache income meter.
0 disables. This is a measurement scaffold — turn it off for a real game.
_bridgeMode: How a cross-branch link is priced. Both rules are live code:
loop     — value is the DETOUR REMOVED between the two ends, measured over
the built network, times a bonus for each single point of failure
it bypasses. Prefers big rings. Up to 8 nodes per link. (v0.26)
shortcut — value is how much the far side's road HOME to the Nest shortens.
Prefers small cuts near the base; will not build a ring between
two equally distant branches. Up to 6 nodes. (v0.25)
off      — links are still planned, ranked, logged and drawn in the viewer,
but none are built. The control arm.
Also available as A/B arms: bridgeloop, bridgeshortcut, bridgeoff.
_rig: The A/B rig. configCycle rotates one arm per round; 'off' means the arms
stop and the knobs below apply instead. Arms: adaptive, ratio2..ratio5,
cap18, bridgeloop, bridgeshortcut, bridgeoff, and ratio3ap.
ratio3ap is ratio3 under a different tag — the anti-pile-up manager changed
the bot, so its rounds must not pool with last night's ratio3.
roundsPerMap holds the same map for that many rounds before the rotation
advances — high on purpose, because arms need identical ground and only
NarakaCity has a single spawn layout.
_testMode: true  — soak: the harness auto-joins, force-ends the round after
endRoundAfterMinutes, cycles the map, and suppressCombat applies.
false — PLAYABLE: no forced round end, no map cycling, aliens fight.
TO PLAY AGAINST THE ALIEN AI, set testMode false. suppressCombat only has
any effect while testMode is true, so leaving it true is harmless then.
_chainExtendPerTick: Unreachable sites whose node chain may be extended in one planner tick.
chainExtendDemandPerTick is a SEPARATE, larger budget for ground shrimps
are already walking to — being late there is paid in long-distance
hauling, so it is never rationed against speculative reaches.
Neither budget touches the blueprint's own planned node chains, so outward
branch expansion is unaffected by both.
Uncapped (v0.31.0) it started a line toward every unreachable site at once:
node construction rose 109 -> 144 per round while Bio Caches stayed at 26,
and the stubs read as over-bridging on the map. 0 disables reach-noding.
_timeScale: Simulation speed. 1 = real time. 2 finishes a 25 game-minute round in about
ASKING FOR 2x DOES NOT GIVE 2x. If the box cannot compute the frames, game
time falls behind and the round becomes a different game rather than a
faster one. [RTSA/TIME] reports the ACHIEVED rate each game-minute and warns
when it is short; serverFps stays a real-time number (unscaled) so it still
Validate before trusting: one 2x round against the 1x baseline of 404k +/-
29k at 25 min. Matching curves = safe. Diverging = keep 1x for measurement.
_tapReachMode: How close the chain must get to a patch before its Bio Cache is placeable.
measured (default) — what the game has actually allowed this round, less a
node's slide (~147m). Correct, but costs about one extra node per site.
optimistic — the pre-v0.37.1 rule, reach + 40m (~249m). Cheaper chains, but
strands a site whenever the last hop lands short of where it was planned.
Switchable so the two can be compared between rounds rather than argued.
_military: THE MILITARY LAYER. Off by default — a DLL swap must never start an army.
Everything here is re-read at map load, so a played evening can tune it
between rounds without stopping the server.
BRING IT UP IN THIS ORDER, one step per round:
1. enabled=true, execute=false — nothing moves. Read [DEFENCE], [MISSION]
and [BATTALION] and check the portfolio picks ground you would defend.
2. execute=true, offence=false — defence only. Watch that the garrison
stays home, that responses ARRIVE TOGETHER rather than trickling, and
that units are not tugged between vanilla and us.
3. offence=true — the army pushes when it stops growing. Expect this one
to be wrong first; it is the least measured thing in the mod.
In-game, /rtsai mil prints the posture, the portfolio and every battalion.
SWITCHES
enabled  — master. false = the layer computes nothing at all.
execute  — issue orders. false = plan and log, touch no unit.
produce  — queue combat units and place higher-tier producers.
offence  — allow push missions. false = defence and garrison only.
PRICING — both are PLACEHOLDERS and both want exchange ratios from
combat.jsonl, which needs two-sided engagements that no soak can produce.
One played game moves these more than a night of AI-vs-AI.
cashPerThreat  — cash a defender is worth per point of threat. Threat is
summed UIAttackRating, so this converts the game's danger
units into the currency every other decision uses.
Raise it and the AI sends more at everything.
strengthMargin — how much MORE than the threat a force must be before it
is sent. Above 1 because trading evenly on defence loses.
ALLOCATION
homeShare         — least of the army that stays home, as a fraction of
army VALUE, so it scales instead of being wrong early
and wrong late. The garrison is a floor and a veto.
maxDefendMissions — simultaneous defences. Beyond a few the army is being
divided into pieces that lose separately.
MONEY. Not a budget share. The economy keeps ecoReserve while it is BEHIND
its worker trajectory and still converting cash into workers that earn; once
it is on track, or yield is falling and the answer is ground not workers,
the military may spend down to zero. Rounds sit on 100-200k unspent from
minute twelve, so that idle bank is what pays for the army.
lesserCystShare — share of Lesser Cysts making combat units instead of
shrimps. Forced to zero while the economy is behind.
PUSH. Fires when army value stops growing WHILE cash is available — money
present and not becoming army means the ceiling is production or population,
and waiting lifts neither. A quiet enemy is NOT a trigger: holding compounds
ahead while unattacked, so inactivity is neutral-to-good.
pushGrowthFloor     — cash/s of army growth below which holding is a loss.
pushMargin          — ours over their estimate before committing.
pushRetreatFraction — fraction of committed peak value at which the push
is called off. Not a timer, not first contact.
NOT BUILT, and deliberately: raids (need enemy-structure discovery we only
just started collecting), formations (cannot be judged before exchange
ratios exist), and the economic-push posture. See MILITARY_TACTICS.md.
_lockAlienCommander: true — the alien commander seat is emptied and handed back to the AI within
a second of any player taking it. Use it whenever you are playing AGAINST
the bot: a human in that seat disables the AI commander, which stands the
eco planner down and silences the whole military layer, and the round
carries on looking normal. [ALIEN/LOCK] logs each ejection.
false (default) — anyone may command the aliens. Required for co-op, where
EcoAssistWithHumanCommander keeps the economy running for a human.
_maxNodeFronts: Hard ceiling on how many fronts may be NODING at once. Applied at all three
places fronts are opened — the per-tick node fire budget, the escape hatch,
and pioneer chains — so it cannot be honoured in one path and ignored in
The planner funds fronts from surplus and opens six or more on a deep bank,
which is right for an eco soak and wrong for a played game, where broad
noding spreads structures a defence cannot cover.
0 (default) — no ceiling, the planner's own budget applies.
_eco: Economy knobs worth changing between rounds.
_rigOwned: Ignored while arms are cycling — see _readme.
